claim: Italian law (Article 2-bis of Legislative Decree 25/2008, the Procedure Decree) lists Bangladesh among Italy's safe countries of origin.
quote: sono considerati Paesi di origine sicuri i seguenti: Albania, Algeria, Bangladesh

claim: Bangladesh was first added to Italy's list of safe countries of origin by a Ministerial Decree of 7 May 2024.
quote: By Ministerial Decree of 7 May 2024, the list of safe countries was expanded to include additional countries: Bangladesh, Cameroon, Colombia, Egypt, Peru and Sri Lanka.

claim: On 24 October 2024 the government issued Decree-Law 158/2024, which wrote the list of safe countries directly into Article 2-bis of the Procedure Decree.
quote: on 24 October 2024, in an attempt to provide a stronger legal basis to the procedure for transferring asylum seekers from safe countries to Albania, the government issued DL 158/2024, which amended Article 2 bis of the Procedure decree to directly include the list of safe countries in the law.

claim: An application from a person from a safe country of origin goes into the accelerated procedure and can be rejected as manifestly unfounded if the person has not shown serious reasons why the country is not safe for them.
quote: In this case the decision rejecting the application is based on the fact that the person concerned has not shown that there are serious reasons to believe that the designated safe country of origin is not safe in relation to their particular situation.

claim: The Questura must tell an applicant from a safe country of origin, when the application is lodged, that it may be rejected.
quote: The Questura shall inform the applicant, at the moment of lodging of the application that if they come from a designated country of safe origin, their application may be rejected.

claim: On 23 February 2026 the Council of the EU formally adopted the first EU-wide list of safe countries of origin.
quote: Today, the Council formally adopted the first EU-wide list of safe countries of origin

claim: The EU list designates Bangladesh, Colombia, Egypt, India, Kosovo, Morocco and Tunisia as safe countries of origin at EU level.
quote: The list designates the following countries as safe countries of origin at EU level: Bangladesh, Colombia, Egypt, India, Kosovo*, Morocco and Tunisia.

claim: The EU safe-country list applies from 12 June 2026, with the rest of the Pact on Migration and Asylum.
quote: will begin to apply on 12 June 2026, at the same time as the rest of the migration and asylum pact.

claim: Member states can keep their own national lists of safe countries alongside the EU list.
quote: Member states will still be able to have their own national lists with additional third countries, which they consider as safe.

claim: The European Commission can suspend a country, or part of its territory or population, from the EU safe list after a substantiated assessment.
quote: An entire country, or part of its territory or population, may be suspended by the European Commission from being designated as safe at the EU level, following a substantiated assessment.

claim: Under the EU Asylum Procedure Regulation, an application is examined in the accelerated procedure if the applicant's nationality has an EU-wide recognition rate of 20% or lower in the latest yearly Eurostat data, unless the person belongs to a category for whom that rate is not representative.
quote: for which the proportion of decisions by the determining authority granting international protection is, according to the latest available yearly Union-wide average Eurostat data, 20 % or lower

claim: The accelerated examination must end no later than three months after the application is lodged.
quote: The determining authority shall conclude the accelerated examination procedure as soon as possible and no later than three months from the date on which the application is lodged.

claim: Under Italy's implementing decree the border procedure is compulsory for people from countries with an acceptance rate below 20%, people who are a danger to national security, and people who gave false information or documents.
quote: The border procedure, in implementation of the provisions of the new Pact, will be compulsory in the case of individuals who are dangerous to national security, who come from countries with an acceptance rate of less than 20%; who have submitted false information or documents.

claim: Italy must examine up to 16,032 applications a year in the border procedure between 12 June 2026 and 12 June 2027.
quote: will have to examine up to 16,032 applications per year in the first period of application between 12 June 2026 and 12 June 2027

claim: During the border procedure the applicant must stay at or near the border or in another designated place, which does not count as entry into Italy.
quote: the applicant is required, as a rule, to stay at or near the external border, in a transit zone or in other places designated by the Member State, without this entailing authorisation to enter the national territory

claim: Decree-Law 100 of 12 June 2026, Italy's first implementation of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, was converted into law without changes by Law 145 of 7 August 2026.
quote: convertito, senza modificazioni, dalla legge 7 agosto 2026, n. 145

claim: The border asylum procedures made mandatory by the Pact must be completed within a maximum of twelve weeks.
quote: che devono essere espletate entro il termine massimo di dodici settimane

claim: In the accelerated border procedure the Territorial Commission must decide and notify its decision within four weeks.
quote: nica la decisione sulla domanda entro quattro settimane.

claim: Against a decision taken in the border procedure, the appeal must be filed within five days of notification and does not suspend the decision, except for unaccompanied minors.
quote: è ammesso ricorso entro cinque giorni decorrenti dalla notificazione. La proposizione del ricorso non sospende l’efficacia esecutiva della decisione

claim: In the border procedure, the applicant can ask the court, together with the appeal, for permission to stay, and cannot be removed while that request is pending.
quote: Il ricorrente può chiedere di essere autorizzato a rimanere con istanza depositata, a pena di inammissibilità, unitamente al ricorso.

claim: In the accelerated cases of Article 67(7)(a) of the Asylum Procedure Regulation, the appeal must be filed within seven days of notification.
quote: inammissibilità, entro sette giorni dalla notificazione del

claim: As a rule an appeal now suspends the rejection, except in the cases of Article 68(3) of the Asylum Procedure Regulation.
quote: La proposizione del ricorso sospende l’effica-
note: Quote is split across a line break in the PDF: continues 'cia esecutiva del provvedimento impugnato, ad eccezione dei casi previsti dall'articolo 68, paragrafo 3'.

claim: Identification checks at the border (screening, fingerprints, Eurodac) must end within a maximum of 72 hours, after which the person is released.
quote: di settantadue ore decorrenti dal momento di cui al primo

claim: Applications lodged before 12 June 2026 continue under the old rules until the case ends.
quote: 4. Ai procedimenti amministrativi o giudiziari avviati
note: Article 17(4): continues 'in data anteriore al 12 giugno 2026, continua ad applicarsi la disciplina previgente'.

claim: Until 31 October 2026 the Questure and border police offices receive, register and formalise all asylum applications.
quote: 31 ottobre 2026, sono in ogni caso competenti a ricevere

claim: When the application is registered, the Questura or border police gives the applicant a named document with a unique identity code, photo and declared personal details.
quote: richiedente protezione internazionale un documento no-
note: Article 4(1) Reception Decree as replaced: 'rilasciano al richiedente protezione internazionale un documento nominativo, recante il codice unico d'identita'.

claim: An asylum seeker may work once ninety days have passed since the application was formalised, if the decision is still pending and the delay is not the applicant's fault.
quote: novanta giorni dalla formalizzazione della domanda
note: Conflicts with AIDA (60 days), which describes the pre-June 2026 rule; DL 100/2026 changed sixty to ninety days.

claim: Decree-Law 100/2026 replaced 'sixty days from the presentation of the application' with 'ninety days from the formalisation of the application' as the waiting time before an asylum seeker may work.
quote: «sessanta giorni dalla presentazione della domanda» sono sostitu-

claim: Before Decree-Law 100/2026, an asylum seeker could start work 60 days after lodging the application; the asylum permit cannot be converted into a work permit.
quote: an asylum applicant can start to work after 60 days from the moment they lodged the asylum application.
note: Pre-Pact rule; current law (Normattiva art. 22) says ninety days from formalisation.

claim: Even after working, an asylum seeker's permit cannot be converted into a work or residence permit.
quote: the asylum applicant permit cannot be converted into a work or residence permit.

claim: Employers are often wary of hiring asylum seekers who hold only the asylum receipt or a renewal request, because these carry no expiry date.
quote: employers are often wary of hiring asylum applicants who are in possession only of the asylum request receipt or the request for renewal of the six-month permit

claim: The 2025 Alace and Canpelli case concerned two Bangladeshis rescued at sea, taken to a detention centre in Albania, whose applications were rejected in the accelerated border procedure because Bangladesh is designated safe.
quote: two Bangladeshi nationals, rescued at sea by the Italian authorities, were taken to a detention centre in Albania

claim: On 1 August 2025 the EU Court of Justice ruled that a safe-country designation made by law must be open to effective judicial review, with its sources accessible to the applicant and the court.
quote: provided that that designation can be subject to effective judicial review

claim: The Court held that, until the new Regulation applies, a country cannot be designated safe if it does not protect certain categories of people; the new Regulation, which allows exceptions for such categories, applies from 12 June 2026.
quote: will be applicable as from 12 June 2026

claim: The Court held that a Member State may not include a country on its safe list if it does not offer adequate protection to its entire population.
quote: a Member State may not include a country in the list of safe countries of origin if that country does not offer adequate protection to its entire population.

claim: Because people held in Albania were mostly from safe countries in the border procedure, the August 2025 ruling directly affected transfers to Albania.
quote: the CJEU decision directly affected transfers to Albania

claim: In 2025 Bangladeshis were the largest group of asylum applicants in Italy: 28,365 applicants, with 37,130 cases pending at year end.
note: Row of table: applicants, pending end 2025, decisions, rejections, refugee, subsidiary, special protection (Eurostat).

claim: In 2025 Italy took 29,595 first-instance decisions on Bangladeshis: 26,240 rejections, 380 refugee status, 155 subsidiary protection and 2,820 special protection.
The 2025 first-instance rejection rate for Bangladeshis in Italy was 88.66%; refugee status went to 1.28% and special protection to 9.53%.
Across all nationalities, Italy's first-instance protection rate in 2025 was 30%.
quote: The overall protection rate (including special protection) at first instance stood at 30%.

claim: Four of the five main nationalities of asylum applicants in Italy in 2025 (Bangladesh, Peru, Egypt, Morocco) are on the national safe list.
quote: Out of the main 5 nationalities of asylum applicants in 2025, Bangladesh, Peru, Pakistan, Egypt and Morocco, 4 are on the national safe country of origin list.

claim: In Q1 2026 Italy took 10,095 first-instance decisions on Bangladeshis, rejecting 8,940.
quote: Q,PER,BD,T,TOTAL,NEG,IT,2026-Q1,8940

claim: In Q2 2026 Italy took 9,660 first-instance decisions on Bangladeshis, rejecting 8,405.
quote: Q,PER,BD,T,TOTAL,NEG,IT,2026-Q2,8405

claim: In Q3 2026 Italy took 8,035 first-instance decisions on Bangladeshis, rejecting 6,720.
quote: Q,PER,BD,T,TOTAL,NEG,IT,2026-Q3,6720

claim: Italy's total first-instance decisions on Bangladeshis: 10,095 in Q1, 9,660 in Q2 and 8,035 in Q3 2026 (27,790 in all).
quote: Q,PER,BD,T,TOTAL,TOTAL,IT,2026-Q3,8035
note: Q1 10095 and Q2 9660 rows in same file; sum 27,790; rejections 24,065 (86.6%).

claim: Of positive decisions for Bangladeshis in Italy in Q1-Q3 2026, refugee status went to 130, 125 and 120 people and humanitarian (special) protection to 985, 1,100 and 1,170.
quote: Q,PER,BD,T,TOTAL,POS_HUM,IT,2026-Q3,1170
note: Refugee rows POS_RFG 130/125/120; subsidiary POS_SPROT 45/30/20; humanitarian POS_HUM 985/1100/1170.

claim: First-time Bangladeshi asylum applicants in Italy were 1,875 in June 2026 and fell to 720 in July, 830 in August and 780 in September 2026.
quote: M,PER,BD,T,FRST,TOTAL,IT,2026-07,720

claim: In January-March 2026, 2,320, 2,125 and 2,320 Bangladeshis made first-time asylum applications in Italy each month.
quote: M,PER,BD,T,FRST,TOTAL,IT,2026-01,2320

claim: In 2025 Bangladeshis were the largest nationality among asylum applications registered with EUAA support in Italy (5,154 of 25,584).
quote: Bangladesh (5,154)

claim: A person already in Italy expresses the intention to apply for asylum at the Immigration Office (Ufficio immigrazione) of the nearest Questura; on arrival, at the Border Police.
quote: If you are already in Italy, at the Immigration office (Ufficio immigrazione) of the nearest Provincial Police Headquarters (Questura).

claim: People in prison or a pre-removal centre also have the right to apply for asylum.
quote: Even if you are in a prison or being held in a pre-removal facility, you have the right to apply for international protection.

claim: At registration the police record personal details and reasons, take a photo and fingerprints (stored in Eurodac), and may ask for the passport.
quote: If you have a passport, you might be requested to hand it over to the Police.

claim: The applicant may hand in a written account of their story, in Italian or another language.
quote: you can also submit a written document (in Italian or another language) in which you explain your story and the reasons for your application.

claim: Interpreting at registration is free.
quote: you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter for free.

claim: Asylum information is confidential and is not shared with the authorities of the country of origin without consent.
quote: will not share any information –without your consent–with any external persons, including authorities of your country of origin.

claim: No lawyer is needed to apply; a lawyer before the Commission is at the applicant's own expense; reception centres and NGOs give free legal support.
quote: many NGOs and associations can also provide you with free legal support.

claim: An appeal requires a lawyer, and people without enough money have the right to a free lawyer before the court.
quote: If your application has been rejected, you can lodge your appeal against this decision. In this case, you need to be assisted by a lawyer.

claim: When the application is filed, the applicant is given the National Commission's 'Practical guide for applicants for international protection in Italy', which exists in 14 languages including Bengali.
quote: amarico; bengali; curdo kurmanji; somalo; tigrino; urdu; farsi; russo; ucraino

claim: An interpreter must be provided at the Questura when the application is recorded on form C3, at the Commission interview and in court.
quote: in Questura, al momento della verbalizzazione della domanda mediante la compilazione

claim: Before the Commission a lawyer is optional and paid by the applicant; in court a lawyer is compulsory and people without means get state-funded legal aid.
quote: accedere al patrocinio a spese dello Stato.

claim: Communications about the procedure must be translated into the applicant's first language or, if not possible, into English, French, Spanish or Arabic.
quote: tra quelle cd. veicolari, che sono l'inglese, il francese, lo spagnolo e l'arabo.

claim: The applicant must attend the personal interview, state all relevant facts and hand over all documents, including the passport.
quote: incluso il passaporto, qualora ne fosse in possesso

claim: The applicant must tell the Questura and the Commission promptly of every change of address; otherwise notices are validly delivered to the last declared address.
quote: concernenti il provvedimento si intendono validamente effettuate presso l'ultimo domicilio

claim: Missing the Commission interview can count as implicit withdrawal of the application.
quote: mancata comparizione al colloquio in termini di ritiro implicito della domanda

claim: The Questore can order an inspection of the applicant's phone and SIM to establish identity, nationality and travel route, for people rescued at sea, caught crossing irregularly or held in a CPR; correspondence and messages are excluded.
quote: sia giunto in Italia a seguito di operazioni di salvataggio in mare; oppure

claim: The asylum form C3 records personal history, the journey and the reasons for leaving; it is signed by the applicant and sent to the Territorial Commission, and the applicant gets a copy.
quote: Asylum applicants receive a copy of the C3 and copies of all other documents submitted to the police authorities.

claim: In big cities formal registration can take place weeks or months after the person asks for asylum, and meanwhile they may have no reception or health care beyond emergencies.
quote: In practice, the formal registration might take place weeks (or months) after the asylum applicant made the asylum application.

claim: When Questure refuse access to the procedure they give no document, exposing people to arrest and deportation; this mainly affects people who apply after living in Italy.
quote: When they prevent access to the procedure, Questure do not issue any document attesting the intention of the persons concerned to seek asylum.

claim: In 2024 the average wait to apply for asylum at the Questure of Vicenza and Venice was 90 to 100 days.
quote: the average waiting time to apply for international protection in the two offices in 2024 being between 90 and 100 days

claim: Under Decree-Law 145/2024, an application made without good reason more than 90 days after irregular entry or the start of irregular stay goes to the accelerated procedure and gives no right to accommodation.
quote: an asylum application submitted – without justified reasons – more than 90 days from the irregular entry in Italy or from the start of the period of irregular stay, is channelled into the accelerated procedure and does not give access to accommodation

claim: Italian law excludes from reception an applicant who, without good reason, applied after the legal time limit.
quote: non è ammesso alle misure di accoglienza il richiedente che, senza giustificato motivo, ha presentato domanda di protezione internazionale oltre il termine

claim: The asylum interview is held only by the Territorial Commission; police cannot examine the merits.
quote: Police authorities cannot examine the merits of the asylum application.

claim: Under the pre-Pact rules the regular procedure could last up to 18 months, and in practice time limits are never respected.
quote: the asylum procedure may last for a maximum period of 18 months.

claim: Appeals against a Territorial Commission decision go to specialised sections of the civil court; the court's decision can only be challenged on points of law at the Court of Cassation within 30 days.
quote: the final decision of the civil court (first appeal) can only be challenged in law before the Court of Cassation (final appeal) within 30 days.

claim: Court cases on asylum appeals often last far longer than the legal 4 months, in some cases tenfold.
quote: the actual duration largely exceeds these terms, in some cases even tenfold.

claim: Under Decree-Law 100/2026, decisions should be taken within 8 months in the ordinary procedure and 4 months in the accelerated procedure.
quote: Decisions should be taken within 8 months under the ordinary procedure or 4 months under the accelerated procedure.

claim: Under Decree-Law 100/2026, appeals must be lodged within 30 calendar days of notification (60 if abroad).
quote: Appeals must be lodged within 30 calendar days from the notification of the first instance decision, or within 60 days if the person stays abroad.

claim: Vulnerable people can now also be put in the accelerated border procedure after an individual assessment.
quote: now accelerated procedures will also apply to vulnerable persons

claim: After 12 June 2026 the Trieste border police began applying the border procedure to people crossing the land border from Slovenia.
quote: the border police of Trieste (included in the maritime border areas) started to apply the border procedure to asylum applicants crossing the internal land border between Italy and Slovenia.

claim: An application can now be treated as implicitly withdrawn in the cases listed in Article 41 of the Asylum Procedure Regulation, with no measure to suspend that decision.
quote: No measure to suspend a withdrawal decision is provided

claim: Repeat (subsequent) applications made only to delay removal, and second or further repeat applications, give no right to stay during the appeal.
quote: A second or further subsequent application made in any Member State following a final decision rejecting a previous subsequent application

claim: Since the Pact entered into force, people in the border procedure have been subject to residence restrictions that in practice amount to detention.
quote: started to be applied to applicants in border procedure in a way that they were de facto detained.

claim: Special protection (protezione speciale) covers people who cannot be expelled because they risk persecution, torture or inhuman treatment, or because of Italy's constitutional and international obligations.
quote: special protection covers cases where people cannot be expelled or refouled as they risk being persecuted

claim: Decree-Law 20/2023 (Law 50/2023) removed the right to ask the Questura directly for special protection and removed protection of private and family life in Italy as a ground.
quote: cancelled the possibility to directly request this kind of permit to a Questura

claim: Special protection permits are granted for two years and are renewable, but since 2023 can no longer be converted into work permits.
quote: These permits are still to be granted for two years and they are renewable but, according to the new law, beneficiaries are not able to transform them in work permits

claim: Refugees and subsidiary protection holders get 5-year permits; special protection holders get 2-year permits; renewals can take 16-18 months.
quote: Refugee status and subsidiary protection beneficiaries are recognised 5-year residence permits, while special protection holders have access 2-year permits.

claim: A rejection, withdrawal or inadmissibility decision of the Territorial Commission also contains a return order and an entry ban, with the effect of an expulsion order.
quote: the decision of the Territorial Commission shall also contain a return order and an entry-ban.

claim: Victims of labour exploitation can get a 'special cases' permit under Article 18-ter of the Consolidated Immigration Act, for six months, renewable for a year.
quote: Victims of labour exploitation

claim: To get a reception place, the applicant must ask for accommodation when applying for asylum, and cannot choose the location.
quote: To access a reception centre, you need to apply for accommodation at the time of your asylum application.

claim: Reception can be withdrawn if the person leaves the centre without authorisation, is violent, or has enough money for independent housing.
quote: Reception measures may be revoked if you decide to leave the center without formal authorization

claim: The ARCI-UNHCR helpline for refugees and asylum seekers is 800 905 570, or +39 3511376335 for Lycamobile/WhatsApp, numeroverderifugiati@arci.it.
quote: 800 905 570 or +39 3511376335 for Lycamobile users/Whatsapp, e-mail numeroverderifugiati@arci.it

claim: If a reception-centre problem is not solved by the manager, the person can contact the local Prefecture.
quote: you can contact the local Prefecture directly.

claim: Asylum seekers in government centres and CAS receive pocket money of EUR 2.50 a day, and there is no allowance outside the reception system.
quote: each asylum applicant hosted in governmental reception centres and CAS receives €2.50 per day.

claim: Since 2023 Italian courses, legal information and job orientation in reception centres are optional services.
quote: considers the following services as purely optional and as mere subcategories of social assistance: Italian language courses

claim: On 31 December 2025, 101,106 asylum seekers were housed in emergency centres (CAS), 3,652 in hotspots and 3,342 in government centres.
quote: As of 31 December 2025, 101,106 asylum applicants were accommodated in emergency accommodation centres (CAS), 3,652 in hotspots 3,342 in Government centres.

claim: On 25 September 2025 an EU-chartered flight returned 29 Bangladeshis, 16 of them from Italy.
quote: Among the returnees, 16 were from Italy, nine from Greece, and four from Cyprus.

claim: The Bangladesh Embassy in Italy said 13 of the 16 deported from Italy had been involved in crimes such as robbery, theft and drug offences.
quote: of the 16 deportees from Italy, 13 had been involved in various crimes

claim: A Bangladesh Embassy official in Greece said that under the new EU rules rejected applicants can no longer move on to another country.
quote: many asylum seekers currently move to another country after their applications are rejected

claim: Italy's Ambassador in Dhaka, Antonio Alessandro, said in November 2025 that thousands of Bangladeshis try to reach Italy irregularly each year, mostly seek asylum with false papers, fail and have to return.
quote: বেশিরভাগ ক্ষেত্রেই তারা জাল কাগজপত্র জমা দিয়ে রাজনৈতিক আশ্রয় চান এবং শেষ পর্যন্ত ব্যর্থ হন।

claim: The Ambassador said about 18,000 Bangladeshis reached Italy by various means in 2025, lured by brokers from districts such as Shariatpur, each paying the equivalent of about EUR 15,000.
quote: একেকজন প্রায় ১৫ হাজার ইউরোর সমপরিমাণ টাকা দালালদের দিয়েছেন।

claim: In May 2026 the Italian Ambassador told a Dhaka meeting that under the EU rules starting June 2026 asylum would become harder and the return of irregular migrants faster.
quote: The upcoming policy will strengthen safe migration while making the repatriation process of irregular migrants faster and more streamlined

claim: Rights groups warn that, with Bangladesh on the EU safe list, many Bangladeshi applications may be deemed manifestly unfounded and dismissed at the outset.
quote: many applications—particularly from Bangladesh—may now be deemed

claim: Only one EU country examines an asylum claim, generally the first EU country entered, and the applicant cannot choose.
quote: generally, the competent country for assessing your asylum application is the first European country you entered.

claim: Across the EU, Bangladeshi asylum applicants had a success rate of only 4% in 2024 (EU data).
quote: The success rate for Bangladeshi applicants in 2024 was only 4%.

claim: Under the pre-Pact rules, applicants in detention or in the accelerated procedure had only 15 or 7 days to appeal and stayed in Italy only if the court separately allowed it.
quote: have only 15 days or 7 days to lodge an appeal

claim: Asylum is for a non-EU citizen who cannot return home because they fear persecution or risk serious harm and cannot get protection from their own country.
quote: cannot return to your country of origin because you fear persecution or risk serious harm, and you are unable to receive protection from your country of origin.
